title: Race calculator
trip.label: Trip
trip.hint: Required: rests and pacing differ a lot between the two
trip.tip: Guided group: the main number is the time your past group days' EP/h give, with your capacity time beside it; on your own: the main number is your capacity time (your walking capacity at AeT: the steep walking windows of your trail runs plus the climbing windows of Baiyue (Taiwan's 100 Peaks) hikes at HR ≥ AeT).
calc.tip: A red * is required. Once everything is filled in, every change recalculates on its own; Calculate recalculates right away. With a season-plan event selected, the inputs and result are saved with that event and come back the next time you pick it.
adv.title: Advanced options
adv.hint: Segments, pacing, altitude, heat: the defaults are fine; open to adjust
chart.title: Segment targets
chart.tip:
Each segment's target pace, power or heart rate along the course.
How to read: distance (km) across, one measure up; the light area is the elevation profile; hover the chart or click the table for a segment's details.
Look for: flats and runnable climbs (3–8 %) by power; steep (> 8 %) or walked climbs by an HR cap; trail descents by neither (control and safety), so they are blank on the power / HR chart; on races > 3 h the HR cap is AeT. On trail the HR cap is one number for the whole race; late in the race HR drops by itself (Kerhervé 2015: about 34 bpm over the race), so don't speed up to reach the cap.
Method: the grade models set each segment's target.
safe: Descent: no power or HR target — control and safety
gap.tip: GAP (grade-adjusted pace): Minetti's formula turns the pace on a slope into the equivalent flat pace. For reference only: it is off on steep climbs, descents and technical ground. A study pooling 674 data sets found Minetti's error largest uphill, and no grade formula has any data on technical terrain (Looney 2025); Koop also treats GAP as a direction only.
gap.note: The GAP column is Minetti's grade adjustment, for reference only: it is off on steep climbs, descents and technical ground (Looney 2025; Koop).
legend.gap_power: gap on the chart = power is only a reference here (steep, descent; grey in the table)
legend.gap_hr: gap on the chart = HR is only a reference on trail descents (grey in the table)
map.hint: hover the map or the profile to see the same point on both; switch basemaps top right
env.title: Conditions
env.tip: From = your usual training conditions (where your power was measured): the median altitude of your last 90 days of runs, temperature and humidity from the historical weather of those runs, else the median of all your activities. To = race day: with an event, date and place (peak, coordinates or the GPX start) the forecast is fetched on its own (CWA mountain forecast → Open-Meteo → the CWA township forecast when Open-Meteo has no data); a date more than 16 days ahead uses the mean of the same month (15 days either side of the race date) over the last 10 years, hour by hour. The difference becomes the environment factor M. Press ✎ to change them.
env.adv: Advanced: change From / To yourself (blue = changed by you; clear to go back to automatic)
env.to_wait: fetched once a date and place are set
env.need_date: fetched once the race date is set
env.need_loc: fetched once a place (peak, coordinates) or a GPX course is set
env.none: No automatic data; press ✎ to fill it in
env.clim_meta: , the same month over {years} years, mean of {models} models, temperature taken to this altitude
env.clim_partial: (some years missing; fetched again next time)
env.clim_hourly: ; includes each hour's mean (cool dawn, warm afternoon), so heat is set per segment
env.town_meta: , township forecast: {name} ({km} km away), temperature moved from the township office's {from} m to {to} m ({dz} m, {dc} °C), humidity unchanged
rain.pop: highest chance of rain in the race window {p} %
night.label: Night
night.tip: With a start time, the segments run between sunset and sunrise at the race location (from the weather forecast, else an astronomical formula) are marked Night and shaded dark on the chart. The night slowdown lengthens only the dark part of each segment; the ETAs and the finish move with it. At 0 % the prediction does not change at all. Not applied in target-time mode.
night.note: No study separates how much darkness alone slows you; Brager 2020's 35.9 % includes fatigue
heat.tip: Once the race-day weather is in and it has hourly data, each segment uses the temperature and dew point at the time you reach it, so a cool morning and a hot midday show in each segment's target. Hourly data come from the CWA 3-day forecast or the Open-Meteo forecast; a date more than 16 days ahead uses each hour's mean over the same month in the last 10 years. On a GPX course each segment's temperature is also moved to its own height (about 0.65 °C cooler per 100 m up, humidity unchanged). When the times change, the arrival times change too, and it recomputes until they settle. Without hourly data (CWA 1-week forecast, offline, weather not fetched yet) or without a start time, one temperature is used for the whole race.
heat.applied_clim: Applied: {n} segments use the hourly mean of the same month over {years} years, {passes} passes
coros.title: Export to plan
coros.tip: Writes this race's legs as one session on race day in your training plan: edit each step on the Schedule page, then push it to the watch from there. On trails the watch's distance is often off (switchbacks, tree cover), so trail and Baiyue (Taiwan's 100 Peaks) exports end every step with the lap button: press lap at the place the step names (aid station, top or bottom of a climb); the name also gives the predicted time and climb. On a road GPS is fine, so road exports use distance steps. Each step's target follows the segment targets: power ± 3 %; steep and walked climbs only an HR cap (no estimated power; open when there is no cap); none on trail descents. Baiyue exports carry heart rate only (no power, no pace); a multi-day Baiyue trip cannot be exported, only a single-day one. The estimated TSS counts legs without a target at the calculator's predicted race HR ÷ LTHR; after each race it is compared with the actual TSS for a personal correction (close to 1 with few races). One session per race: exporting again overwrites the last export.
coros.same: The plan already has this version
coros.claim: replaces the plan's “Race” session on that day
coros.restored: you deleted this session from the plan; it will be added back
coros.edited: This session was changed on the Schedule page: exporting overwrites your changes
coros.confirm_overwrite: This race session was changed on the Schedule page; exporting overwrites your changes. Overwrite?
coros.need_event: Pick the target race first: the export goes on that race's day
coros.push_hint: Once it is in the plan, push it to the watch from the Schedule page
coros.old_watch: The watch has this race from an earlier direct export: it is replaced the next time this session is pushed from the plan
coros.tss_hr: legs without a target at IF {f} ({src})
coros.tss_default: no HR prediction: legs without a target at the default IF {f}
coros.tss_nocalib: no post-race correction yet (compared with the actual TSS after each race)
pick.title: Pick a location on the map
pick.hint: Click the map to drop a marker; drag it to fine-tune. Switch basemaps top right. A click within 300 m of a known peak also takes the peak's elevation.
goal.tip: Enter the goal as a pace (average pace or finish time) or as a power (average power in W or % CP): both are offered. The per-km / segment targets are spread from your goal by the grade model. No goal = the model's own prediction.
goal.vs_tip: Model = the 「model prediction」 time (100 % effort) on the same course and weather. Faster by more than 3 % is flagged, by more than 8 % warned; the thresholds are an estimate.
goal.fast: {pct}% faster than the model: may not hold
goal.too_fast: {pct}% faster than the model: likely won't hold
zbar.axis_power: Palladino; axis = % CP, line = this race's average power
zbar.axis_hr: axis = heart rate in bpm, line = this race's predicted average heart rate
zbar.tip: This bar shows absolute intensity: which of your zones the race's average power or heart rate falls in. The effort bar above shows relative intensity: how long you can hold this power, which depends on the race length — 85% CP is easy for 1 hour and hard for 8 hours. Each colour is a zone (each zone's name and range are listed below); the line is this race's average. Power training shows power zones, heart-rate training shows heart-rate zones (the training basis in Settings); you can pick the heart-rate zone model, the default is the workout heart-rate zones in Settings.
zbar.line_power: Absolute intensity: average {pct} CP ({w}), in Palladino zone {zone}
zbar.line_hr: Absolute intensity: average {hr} bpm, in {sys} zone {zone}
zbar.no_hr_data: This calculation has no average heart rate, so the power zones are shown
surface.label: Trail surface
surface.meta: Flats and descents use your own dry / wet technicality factor (from {dry} stretches of 100 m marked dry and {wet} marked wet; estimate). No choice = as before, dry and wet data pooled
surface.meta_hr: The whole-race time still comes from the heart-rate model; the surface only changes how it is split: "wet" gives descents and flats more of the time (from {dry} stretches of 100 m marked dry and {wet} marked wet; estimate)
strategy.tip: Even pace (road): the same average power all the way. Even effort (trail): the same effort all the way; on hills the power follows the hill flexibility below, so the pace changes with the grade rather than staying one pace. Negative / positive split: the power changes linearly from start to finish with the same race average. Most studies find the smallest spread between the halves fastest.
legend.hr_fade: Late in the race your HR drops by itself; don't speed up to reach the cap
fade: segment times follow your own pace change over the hours (estimate)
cad.title: Climbing cadence
cad.how: Counts only moving time with cadence on the 100 m stretches of 3 % or steeper, in your outdoor runs of the last year. Every walk / run split in the app is “cadence below 130 spm = walking”; on climbs cadence usually falls into a walking and a running group, and the line should sit in the valley between them. This only checks; it never moves the line.
rw.title: Walk–run transition speed
rw.default: Default values, none of your data yet: a grade needs at least 10 walked and 10 run windows.
rw.personal: Your transition speed is {d} m/s off the default ({n} windows, shrunk towards the default). The calculator's walk / run labels use it.
rw.how: Slower than the line, walking costs less; faster, running does. The default line comes from treadmill tests on high-level male runners (Brill & Kram 2021, Ortiz 2017); using it for everyone is an estimate. Your line: for every 2 % of grade, the speed at which half of your own 100 m windows are walked and half run; the median difference from the default, shrunk towards 0 by sample size and held within ±0.4 m/s (all estimates). Heart-rate crossovers are not used.
rw.legend_default: walk / run labels: default transition speed
rw.legend_you: walk / run labels: your transition speed
charts.road: Not used for road races: these charts are for trail climbing (grade, walk / run, climbing cadence) and load for trail races.
charts.neterr: The connection dropped before the data arrived (the first time it is computed from a whole year of activities and can take a few minutes).
ptrain.label: Enter it as training-conditions power (multiplied by the environment factor M)
ptrain.tip: Checked: the power you enter is what you hold in your usual training conditions; the calculator multiplies it by this race's environment factor M (altitude, temperature and humidity against your training; with segments, the distance-weighted mean of their M) to get the race-day power, then computes the finish time. E.g. 250 W at M 0.96 → 240 W on race day; %CP works the same. Unchecked: the number is the race-day power as it is.
formula.tip: Trail “Model prediction”: the finish time comes from the heart-rate pace model, which uses your own fitted climb divisor; this option only changes the comparison numbers, the RE details and the average power shown. Target power: the finish time is computed from this effort km, so changing it changes the finish time. Target time: the finish time is your target; changing it changes the average power needed. Without a heart-rate model, the model prediction uses this formula too.
sg.line: Walk or run by the predicted speed (SP-229, not used in predictions yet): trail segment |error| {a} → {b}, climbs {c} → {d} ({n} segments, gait changed on {k}).
sg.no: worse: predictions keep the majority gait
bt.th.title: Trail HR pace model back-test (race HR level, estimate)
bt.th.note: Positive = predicted slower than actual. The shape of the durability decay only shows in long races: compare whether the races ≥ {h} h have the smaller error with or without decay.
bt.th.none: No races of {h} h or longer: the decay shape for long races cannot be validated
snow.label: Snow
snow.tip: Snow time for winter mountains (rule of thumb, Japanese guides): climbs × 1.5 on a tracked trail, × 2–3 with no track. Only the climbs are multiplied; descents and flats stay the same
snow.note_trodden: Snow, tracked: climbing time × 1.5 (rule of thumb, Japanese guides), moving {t} ({base} without snow)
snow.note_untrodden: Snow, no track: climbing time × 2 to × 3 (rule of thumb, Japanese guides), moving {lo} (× 2) to {hi} (× 3), clock {clo} to {chi}; the numbers above use × 2
snow.season: Yushan main-peak trail snow-season rules (about mid-December to March, when Paiyun or Baimulin has ≥ 5 cm of snow): one-day ascents are suspended; crampons, an ice axe and a helmet are required, plus snow experience
sleep.changed: Sleep-point default changed: a new sleep point now gets minutes by the predicted race length (< 36 h 20 min, 36–60 h 30 min, > 60 h 90 min; Kishi 2024, Martin 2018). A blank sleep point here still counts 90 minutes, as before
sleep.changed_now: ; the new default for this race is {m} minutes
accl.tip: Unacclimatised: just arrived; aerobic capacity falls about 6.3% per 1000 m (from 300 m). Acclimatised: the more optimistic altitude curve. Partly acclimatised = the midpoint of the two, an estimate (no study has measured partial acclimatisation). For a Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) trip with nothing picked: 2 or more nights slept above 2,750 m in the 14 days before the trip (activities, plus the nights up high recorded on the schedule calendar) default to partly acclimatised, otherwise unacclimatised; acclimatised only when you pick it. A route topping out under 3,000 m has no partly acclimatised option.
accl.default_partial: Default partly acclimatised: {n} nights above 2,750 m in the 14 days before the trip (estimate)
accl.default_none: Default unacclimatised: {n} nights above 2,750 m in the 14 days before the trip (2 or more for partly acclimatised)
